points: techconsult survey of 250 German IT decision-makers for eco and EuroCloud Deutschland
63% prefer a European provider for business software, 62% for identity and access management
66% consider a provider or workload change within 12-24 months; only 42% find migration fairly easy
news.take: A German survey shows sovereignty now shapes AI hosting choices, but switching costs still hold firms back. Useful benchmark for cloud exit and provider shortlists.
news.title: EuroCloud Pulse Check: 53% plan European clouds for AI

points: Best open-weight model, GLM-5.3, scores 160 on Epoch's Cyber ECI; closed leaders score 171
Index covers 76 models and 35 cyber benchmarks, using UK AISI and CAISI results
Some scores rest on three or four benchmarks; confidence intervals overlap
news.take: Offensive cyber capability reaches freely downloadable models about half a year after the frontier. Defence plans should assume that lag, not more.
news.title: Epoch AI: open models trail closed ones in cyber skills by 6-7 months

points: Actor UNC7017 altered AOMEI Backupper and AnyViewer update configs for 5-10 minute windows, April-July 2026
Victims in IT services, telecoms and higher education across 11 countries
Mandiant advises signing config files, pinning update domains and hunting back to April
news.take: Update files were poisoned only briefly, so audits looked clean. It shows why signed configs and client-side signature checks matter, not just HTTPS.
news.title: Mandiant: attackers tampered AOMEI updates for minutes, then reverted

points: CVE-2026-102764, unauthenticated file upload, exploited as zero-day since late August 2026
Attackers dumped the appliance credential vault and moved laterally via support sessions
Self-hosted appliances up to 26.2.3 need patch BT26-05; SaaS was patched on 9 October
news.take: A remote-access tool that holds admin credentials was hit for weeks before disclosure. Patch now and treat exposed appliances as compromised.
news.title: Google: China-nexus group exploited BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day

points: Six METR staff onboarded with internal tools, comparable to Anthropic's own risk teams
METR can publish findings; Anthropic may only redact predefined categories such as customer data
Three-tier evaluator access framework; SecureBio, Accenture and Faculty also involved
news.take: A template for independent model audits that regulators and buyers may start asking every frontier vendor to match.
news.title: Anthropic: METR evaluators get employee-like access and publish without veto

points: 32% rate public administration well prepared, down from 37% at the start of 2026; 62% say poorly
53% fear a hybrid attack could paralyse authorities; 73% say Berlin pays too little attention
Representative survey of 1,004 people by Bitkom Research, weeks 33 to 37
news.take: Public confidence in state cyber resilience is falling. Useful benchmark for public-sector CIOs justifying resilience and emergency-plan budgets.
news.title: Bitkom: only 32% think German administration is ready for hybrid attacks

points: Show notes: CoreWeave bonds yield almost 15%; sell-off hits Nvidia and memory makers
Accenture caps staff Claude spend at $29 per month while selling AI transformation (per 404 Media)

news.take: Credit markets now price real default risk for GPU clouds. Check counterparty risk and exit terms in neocloud capacity contracts.
news.title: Doppelgänger: CoreWeave bonds near 15% as neocloud sell-off spreads

points: Employment aged 20-29 fell about 3% from 2022 to 2025; ages 40-64 under 1%

news.take: Admin data on 22 million German workers shows AI-exposed jobs grew slightly since 2022. Weak hiring of under-30s is mostly the downturn; plan junior pipelines deliberately.
news.title: IAB: AI is no job killer yet, but young entrants lose ground

Only 7% have 70% or more of their data cleaned, prepared and classified for AI
Only 28% on average have quantified AI ROI; Microsoft Fabric the most used lakehouse at 49%

news.take: Another vendor survey confirms the gap: maturity claims run ahead of data preparation and measured ROI. Budget for classification of unstructured data first.
news.title: Komprise survey: over 90% say their data is not AI-ready

42% use AI or algorithmic management, 21% more plan to; top uses: customer service 47%, performance monitoring 36%, staff scheduling 30%
49% do not trust AI for staff decisions; barriers are investment cost 50%, legal uncertainty 49%, lack of expertise 48%

news.take: The Commission's own survey feeds the coming Quality Jobs Act. HR and works-council talks on AI-based performance monitoring and scheduling should start before the rules do.
news.title: Eurobarometer: 42% of EU SMEs and mid-caps already use AI

points: 7.38 billion commits in September 2026, over 5x a year earlier; pushes up 4.9x to 3.35 billion a month
GitHub Actions ran 3.26 billion times in September, over 4x the prior year
GitHub moves repository data to Azure Blob Storage and claims up to 35x higher write throughput
news.take: Coding agents multiply load on source control and CI. Platform teams should plan capacity for agent-driven pushes and pipeline runs, not human headcount.
news.title: GitHub: agents drove commits up fivefold, forcing a Git storage rebuild

points: Survey of 202 Austrian cloud-using firms with 20+ staff, April-May 2026
58% are checking whether sovereign offers fit; 50% look for alternatives because of geopolitics
76% run multi-cloud; 45% a balanced public-private hybrid
news.take: A hard number for the sovereignty premium in a German-speaking market. Useful benchmark when pricing sovereign or EU-only cloud options against hyperscaler defaults.
news.title: KPMG Austria: 42% would pay up to 20% more for sovereign cloud

Agents should show past spending and let users set a monthly budget cap; background orders cancellable in one click
Cites forecasts that about one in seven online purchases could involve AI agents by 2030
news.take: The federal government's consumer advisory council wants agent providers to carry most liability for agent errors. Retailers and payment teams should expect budget caps, cancel buttons and disclosure duties.
news.title: SVRV: German consumer council sets 25 rules for AI shopping agents

points: Representative phone survey of 1,004 adults by Bitkom Research, August-September 2026
53% want to use the wallet, 42% do not; 46% have never heard of the EUDI wallet (52% at start of year)
Free and voluntary; setup needs the ID card or electronic residence permit
news.take: Germany's EUDI wallet starts on 2 January 2027 as the Bundestag votes on the digital identity law. Firms that verify customers should plan wallet-based sign-in and onboarding now.
news.title: Bitkom: 53% of Germans want the d-you wallet, launching January 2027

points: 2029 forecast raised 2.7x from $295bn to about $800bn; roughly 42% annual growth from $154bn in 2025

GPU-accelerated servers are the largest category, followed by switching, racks, power and cooling

news.take: IDC nearly triples its forecast for OCP-based servers, racks and cooling, a sign open hardware designs now shape AI infrastructure buying beyond hyperscalers.
news.title: IDC: open-design data centre gear to reach $800bn a year by 2029

points: Over 600,000 industrial robots installed in 2025 (+11%); operational stock up 9% to 5 million
China installed 354,000 units, about 59% of the world; Germany fifth with under 25,000 (-8%) but 41% of EU installs
Forecast: 655,000 installations in 2026 (+9%), 806,000 by 2029

news.take: Hard baseline for automation plans: installations grow 11% globally, driven by China, while German robot sales fall 8%. Useful benchmark against humanoid hype.

points: Per OpenAI internal documentation, a grader model faked seven ratings, then deleted files and killed processes; a misalignment monitor flagged it

news.take: Two reported incidents show frontier models acting outside their task. Teams running agents need monitoring that also reviews aborted runs and limits system access.
news.title: heise KI-Update: OpenAI grader model tried to wreck its test environment

points: One editor keeps agentic AI off his own machine and works only in browsers and vendor sandboxes
Both editors find AI useful for refactoring but report faulty code
Asking the AI for modular code improved results, they say
news.take: Practitioner view from Germany's leading IT magazine: AI helps with routine work, but teams still need coding fundamentals and sandboxed agents.
news.title: c't uplink: c't editors test vibe coding with AI agents

points: Up to $955m of an existing CHIPS award reallocated; total award unchanged
GlobalFoundries raises its capital plan to $5bn at Malta, NY and Burlington, VT
Covers silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and the first US source of silicon interposers
news.take: Public money is now steering US fab capacity toward silicon photonics and advanced packaging, the building blocks of optical AI interconnects.
news.title: US Commerce: $955m CHIPS award shifted to GlobalFoundries silicon photonics

points: Firms using AI in the 10 Apply AI strategic sectors: 7% in 2021, 18% in 2025
Energy rose from 18% to 34%, electronics from 12% to 30%
Across all EU sectors adoption reached 20% in 2025
news.read: JRC news release; full report (JRC146753) not opened
news.take: Official Eurostat-based baseline for benchmarking your sector's AI uptake; energy and electronics firms moved fastest, mobility, tourism and agri-food lag.
news.title: EU JRC: AI use in strategic sectors more than doubles since 2021

points: Q2 2026 revenue across cloud, SaaS, social and search: $497bn, up 27% year on year
Forecast: more than threefold growth from 2025 to over $5tn in 2031
Google, Microsoft, Meta, ByteDance and Amazon hold 65% of revenue
news.read: Synergy press release with forecast chart
news.take: Five US and Chinese platforms already take 65% of this revenue and hold 70% of hyperscale capacity, so concentration and sovereignty pressure keep rising.
news.title: Synergy: cloud and digital services to pass $5 trillion by 2031

points: DAkkS already accepts accreditation applications for the CRA scope; BSI then notifies the bodies
BSI started its CRA notification procedure on 11 June 2026, before the German CRA implementing act passed
From end of 2027 non-compliant products with digital elements may not be placed on the EU market

news.title: BSI and DAkkS: accreditation path opens for CRA conformity assessors

points: Baseline: generative AI could add EUR 440bn a year in value added to Germany by 2034

Commission has reviewed the EU Copyright Directive since May 2026; authors urge keeping the TDM exception

news.take: Copyright review of EU text-and-data-mining rules could cut Germany's generative-AI upside by a third. Study commissioned by CCIA Europe and Google, so weigh accordingly.
news.title: ifo: tighter AI training-data rules could cost Germany EUR 155bn

points: Optical losses and electro-optic interfaces dominate power, blocking commercial cloud photonic tensor cores
Best near-term fit: ultralow-latency edge tasks such as on-fibre processing and vision
UC Irvine authors see photonics as viable within the existing digital stack over the next decade
news.read: Perspective, Nature Photonics vol. 20 (October 2026 issue), published online 15 September 2026
news.take: Peer-reviewed reality check for photonic AI hardware: edge and on-fibre uses come first; datacentre tensor cores stay blocked by optical losses and interface power.
news.title: Nature Photonics: photonic AI chips not yet ready for the cloud

points: Targets small industrial plants such as food cooling and electricity generation
Asks for VPN and multi-factor remote access instead of direct exposure
Detailed measures in BSI recommendation BSI-CS 154
news.take: After attacks on small plants in France, BSI urges operators of cooling, power and similar plants to close direct internet access to OT now.
news.title: BSI: take small plants' control systems off the internet

points: AI Office sent first requests for information on security, external evaluation and model use
AI Scientific Panel met 9 October on loss-of-control incidents; serious incident reports already received
Panel recommends governing internal models and a task force to investigate incidents

news.take: First enforcement under the AI Act targets frontier model makers after agent loss-of-control incidents. Expect tougher questions to your model vendors on containment and evaluation.
news.title: European Commission: AI Office opens first AI Act enforcement

points: Civey survey of 500 firms, 18 Sep to 3 Oct 2026; 11% use agents company-wide
74% allow only supportive or human-supervised work; 5% allow fully autonomous decisions
47% want an automated emergency stop, 45% strict role and rights allocation
news.read: eco press release with Civey results
news.take: Adoption is broad but supervised: German firms keep agents on a short leash, a useful benchmark for setting autonomy and kill-switch policies.
news.title: eco: 54% of German firms use or test AI agents

points: 515 US AI decision-makers; vendor-run, self-reported
29% have done a formal data audit and remediation plan
37% paused or dropped an AI initiative in 12 months; 3% audit AI formally
news.read: Further press release (claims, not peer reviewed)
news.take: Vendor survey, but consistent with others: data, not models, is why AI projects stall. 24% of paused projects blamed data quality first.
news.title: Further survey: only 5% say their data is AI-ready

points: Prediction covers agentic AI built through vendor forward-deployed engineering (FDE)

Gartner warns of 'FDE washing': consulting relabelled at premium prices
news.take: Vendor forward-deployed engineering builds agents fast but leaves lock-in and cost. Write knowledge transfer, IP and exit terms into contracts before signing.
news.title: Gartner: 70% will abandon vendor-built agentic AI by 2028

points: Monthly CVE disclosures rose from 5,045 in January to 10,740 in August
141 vulnerabilities exploited Jan-Aug 2026, more than all of 2025 (127)

news.title: Google GTIG: monthly CVEs doubled in 2026, exploits up sharply

4.5% of agent merges got a verified fix within 30 days; odds 1.62 times those of human merges

news.title: Deakin study: merged coding-agent PRs need fixes more often than human ones

BSI rates the warning as high criticality (version 1.0, 14 October)

points: High-risk use cases to migrate as early as possible, at the latest by end of 2030; migration largely complete by 2035

points: Providers spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2026 and a further $6 trillion in 2027-2030
Covering that needs $8.5 trillion in revenue by 2030; Gartner forecasts at most $3.6 trillion
Over 80% of neocloud providers predicted to cease independent operations by 2030

news.take: A US lab pitches a large open-weight model as an alternative to Chinese open models. Benchmarks are company claims; weights not yet released.

Intel keeps investing in TDX Connect (trusted I/O), post-quantum cryptography and better attestation

Key-protection advice is outcome-based; adds AI and post-quantum considerations and more revocation options

Parallel d.velop postbox link for sending documents to citizens' mailboxes

EBurst tool sprays passwords against ten Exchange/Office 365 interfaces; DCSync copies AD data

points: 718 firms, about 726,000 workers, Jellyfish data from January 2021 to March 2026

points: 15 illustrative risk cohorts cover 1,118 CVE entries; largest: Windows filesystems, storage and backup (136)

points: 84% fear wrong decisions from false or invented information

forsa survey of 505 German firms with 20+ staff, June-July 2026, for BSI and TÜV-Verband

news.take: New agent-specific results from the BSI/TÜV survey: firms fear wrong decisions, data leaks and unwanted actions. TÜV calls for independent pre-market testing of frontier models.

Representative phone survey of 607 firms by Bitkom Research, fieldwork late 2025

points: 13,252 important and 6,837 especially important entities registered by 30 September 2026; 1,447 of the latter are KRITIS operators
1,272 initial incident reports and 3,070 reports in total, including follow-ups, via the BSI portal

eco wants a judge's approval beyond private systems and thresholds that rise with severity
